previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy was admitted after developing hypotension and chest pain during hemodialysis. She presented with altered mental status, which resolved, and was found to have leukocytosis. A urine culture identified Klebsiella pneumoniae, confirming a urinary tract infection. She received a single dose of intravenous vancomycin in the emergency department and was transitioned to oral antibiotics for home. Her hypotension improved after holding antihypertensive medications, and her condition stabilized. Warfarin was adjusted to increase INR to therapeutic levels. She was discharged home with services the following day in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, monitor weight, adhere to a low-sodium diet, and follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST PORTABLE AP.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Evaluate for pneumonia, CHF.

In comparison to the previous chest radiograph dated ___ the
position of the right- sided internal jugular dual-lumen hemodialysis catheter
is unchanged with the tip at the cavoatrial junction.  There is slight upper
lobe venous congestion with lower lobe septal lines.  No pleural effusion,
consolidation, or pneumothorax.  Tortuosity of the thoracic aorta is noted.
The heart size is normal.

IMPRESSION:  Appearances are consistent with mild pulmonary congestion.  No
consolidation, mass, or pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  ___ female with headache.  Evaluate for hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  ___.

NON-CONTRAST HEAD CT:  There is no hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or CT
evidence of recent infarction.  The grey-white matter differentiation is
preserved.  There are unchanged confluent periventricular white matter
hypodensities, consistent with mild chronic small vessel disease. Lacunar
infarct is seen in the left basal ganglia.  Ventricles and sulci are unchanged
in caliber, again mildly prominent, suggesting underlying parenchymal atrophy.
There is no shift of midline structures.  The basilar cisterns are preserved.
There are no abnormal extra-axial fluid collections. Osseous structures
demonstrate no suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions and no fractures.
Calcifications of the cavernous and supraclinoid internal carotid arteries.
Small fluid level is seen in the sphenoid sinuses.  Remainder of the paranasal
sinuses is well aerated.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.  Chronic small vessel infarcts,
mild parenchymal atrophy, and vascular calcifications are unchanged.
